standard_text: Numbers up to 100 000: place values, reading and writing, comparing and ordering, patterns
meta_desc: Free P4 maths practice on numbers to 100 000: place value, numerals and words, expanded form, comparing, ordering and patterns. 100 questions with answers.

body_html:
Place value to 100 000

Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right. After the thousands comes the ten thousands place. 10 thousands make 10 000, and 10 ten thousands make 100 000 (one hundred thousand).

In a place value chart, TTh = ten thousands, Th = thousands, H = hundreds, T = tens and O = ones.

Place value discs show the same idea. Find the value of each group of discs, then add.

Reading and writing numbers in words

Split off the last three digits. Read the thousands first and say “thousand”. Then read the last three digits. After the thousands, a numeral always has three more digits, so use 0 to hold an empty place.

NumeralsWords
40 503forty thousand, five hundred and three
70 045seventy thousand and forty-five
62 500sixty-two thousand, five hundred
100 000one hundred thousand
Words to numerals

Write fifty thousand and six in numerals.

fifty thousand → 50; six → 006.

Answer: 50 006 (not 5006)

Value of a digit and expanded form

The digit is the symbol. Its value depends on its place. In 37 845 the digit 7 is in the thousands place, so its value is 7000, not 7.

Expanded form shows the value of every digit: 62 708 = 60 000 + 2000 + 700 + 8.

Comparing and ordering

First count the digits: a 5-digit number is greater than any 4-digit number. If the numbers have the same number of digits, compare place by place from the left until two digits are different.

Compare

30 605 ☐ 30 650

Ten thousands: 3 = 3. Thousands: 0 = 0. Hundreds: 6 = 6. Tens: 0 < 5.

Answer: 30 605 < 30 650

Number patterns

To count on in thousands, add 1 to the thousands digit. To count on in ten thousands, add 1 to the ten thousands digit. When the thousands go past 9, rename 10 thousands as 1 ten thousand.

Count on in thousands

47 500, 48 500, 49 500, ☐

49 500 + 1000: 9 thousands + 1 thousand = 10 thousands = 1 ten thousand.

Answer: 50 500

In word problems, draw a bar model to see what to find.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Leaving out zeros (forty thousand, five hundred and three → 4053 or 4503)Write three digits after the thousands: 40 | 503 → 40 503
Giving the digit, not its value (the 7 in 37 845 is 7)It is in the thousands place: 7000
Counting the discs (3 + 2 + 1 = 6)Add the values: 30 000 + 200 + 1 = 30 201
Comparing the first digits only (9876 > 10 234)Count the digits first: 10 234 > 9876
Forgetting to rename in a pattern (49 500 + 1000 → 40 500)10 thousands make 1 ten thousand: 50 500

faq.q: What is taught in P4 whole numbers?
faq.a: Primary 4 students read and write numbers up to 100 000 in numerals and in words, find the value of each digit, compare and order numbers, and continue number patterns. They also round numbers and learn factors and multiples.

faq.q: How do you write forty thousand, five hundred and three in numerals?
faq.a: Write 40 for the thousands and 503 for the rest: 40 503. After the thousands there must always be three digits, so zeros hold the empty places.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with numbers to 100 000?
faq.a: The most common mistake is leaving out zeros, such as writing 40 503 as 4053. Another is giving the digit instead of its value: the 7 in 37 845 is worth 7000.

faq.q: Is numbers to 100 000 in the MOE syllabus?
faq.a: Yes. Numbers up to 100 000, including place value, reading and writing, comparing and ordering, and number patterns, are part of Whole Numbers in the MOE 2021 Primary 4 Mathematics syllabus.

items.q: Which place is the red digit in?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands. In 52 438 the red 5 is in the ten thousands place.

items.q: Which place is the red digit in?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands. In 73 951 the red 3 is in the thousands place.

items.q: What number does the place value chart show?
items.e: Read the digits from the ten thousands to the ones: 4, 0, 5, 0, 3. Keep every 0: it holds an empty place. The number is 40 503.

items.q: How many thousands make 10 000?
items.e: Count in thousands: 1000, 2000 … 10 000. That is 10 thousands. Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right.

items.q: What number do the place value discs show?
items.e: Find the value of each group: 3 × 10 000 = 30 000; 2 × 1000 = 2000. Add them: 32 000. Write 0 in every empty place. Do not just count the discs: each disc has its own value.

items.q: In 47 532, which digit is in the thousands place?
items.e: In 47 532: ten thousands 4, thousands 7, hundreds 5, tens 3, ones 2. The thousands digit is 7.

items.q: Which place is the red digit in?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands. In 41 527 the red 5 is in the hundreds place.

items.q: What number do the place value discs show?
items.e: Find the value of each group: 2 × 10 000 = 20 000; 4 × 100 = 400; 1 × 1 = 1. Add them: 20 401. Write 0 in every empty place. Do not just count the discs: each disc has its own value.

items.q: What number does the place value chart show?
items.e: Read the digits from the ten thousands to the ones: 7, 0, 0, 8, 0. Keep every 0: it holds an empty place. The number is 70 080.

items.q: In 60 295, which digit is in the hundreds place?
items.e: In 60 295: ten thousands 6, thousands 0, hundreds 2, tens 9, ones 5. The hundreds digit is 2.

items.q: What is the greatest 5-digit number?
items.e: Put the greatest digit, 9, in all 5 places: 99 999. 100 000 has 6 digits and 9999 has only 4.

items.q: Which place is the red digit in?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands. In 93 164 the red 6 is in the tens place.

items.q: What number do the place value discs show?
items.e: Find the value of each group: 1 × 10 000 = 10 000; 3 × 10 = 30; 2 × 1 = 2. Add them: 10 032. Write 0 in every empty place. Do not just count the discs: each disc has its own value.

items.q: What number is 3 ten thousands, 4 thousands and 5 tens?
items.e: 30 000 + 4000 + 50 = 34 050. Write a digit for every place: 3, 4, 0, 5, 0.

items.q: In 38 614, which digit is in the tens place?
items.e: In 38 614: ten thousands 3, thousands 8, hundreds 6, tens 1, ones 4. The tens digit is 1.

items.q: What is the smallest 5-digit number?
items.e: A 5-digit number cannot start with 0, so put 1 in the ten thousands place and 0 in all the other places: 10 000. 9999 has only 4 digits.

items.q: What number do the place value discs show?
items.e: Find the value of each group: 4 × 10 000 = 40 000; 1 × 1000 = 1000; 3 × 10 = 30. Add them: 41 030. Write 0 in every empty place. Do not just count the discs: each disc has its own value.

items.q: What number does the place value chart show?
items.e: Read the digits from the ten thousands to the ones: 3, 0, 6, 0, 4. Keep every 0: it holds an empty place. The number is 30 604.

items.q: What number is 6 ten thousands, 7 hundreds and 2 ones?
items.e: 60 000 + 700 + 2 = 60 702. There are no thousands or tens, so write 0 in those places.

items.q: What number is 1 more than 99 999?
items.e: 99 999 + 1: every 9 becomes 0 as you rename, and a 1 goes in the hundred thousands place: 100 000 (one hundred thousand). (99 998 is 1 less.)

sets.title: Reading and writing numbers in words

items.q: How do you write 30 000 in words?
items.e: Split off the last three digits: 30 | 000. Read the thousands, then the rest: 30 → thirty thousand; 000 → nothing more. So 30 000 is “thirty thousand”. 30 000 is 30 thousands. Thirty is 30; thirteen is 13.

items.q: How do you write 45 000 in words?
items.e: Split off the last three digits: 45 | 000. Read the thousands, then the rest: 45 → forty-five thousand; 000 → nothing more. So 45 000 is “forty-five thousand”.

items.q: Which number is forty thousand?
items.e: After the thousands, always write three digits: forty thousand → 40; nothing more → 000. So the number is 40 000. Forty thousand is 40 thousands: 40 followed by 000.

items.q: Which number is forty thousand, five hundred and three?
items.e: After the thousands, always write three digits: forty thousand → 40; five hundred and three → 503. So the number is 40 503. 4053 and 4503 leave out a zero that holds an empty place.

items.q: How do you write 40 503 in words?
c: forty thousand, five hundred and three
forty thousand, five hundred and thirty
four thousand, five hundred and three
items.e: Split off the last three digits: 40 | 503. Read the thousands, then the rest: 40 → forty thousand; 503 → five hundred and three. So 40 503 is “forty thousand, five hundred and three”. The 0s hold empty places: 40 thousands, then 503.

items.q: Which number is seventy thousand and twenty-five?
items.e: After the thousands, always write three digits: seventy thousand → 70; twenty-five → 025. So the number is 70 025.

items.q: 60 300 = sixty thousand, ☐ hundred. Which word goes in the box?
items.e: Split off the last three digits: 60 | 300. Read the thousands, then the rest: 60 → sixty thousand; 300 → three hundred. So 60 300 is “sixty thousand, three hundred”.

items.q: How do you write 70 045 in words?
c: seventy thousand, four hundred and fifty
seventy thousand, four hundred and five
items.e: Split off the last three digits: 70 | 045. Read the thousands, then the rest: 70 → seventy thousand; 045 → forty-five. So 70 045 is “seventy thousand and forty-five”.

items.q: Which number is nineteen thousand, five hundred?
items.e: After the thousands, always write three digits: nineteen thousand → 19; five hundred → 500. So the number is 19 500. Nineteen is 19; ninety is 90.

items.q: Which number is one hundred thousand?
items.e: One hundred thousand is 100 thousands: 100 | 000 = 100 000. It is 1 more than 99 999. (10 000 is ten thousand.)

items.q: How do you write 62 500 in words?
c: six thousand, two hundred and fifty
sixty thousand, two hundred and fifty
items.e: Split off the last three digits: 62 | 500. Read the thousands, then the rest: 62 → sixty-two thousand; 500 → five hundred. So 62 500 is “sixty-two thousand, five hundred”.

items.q: Which number is thirty thousand, four hundred and one?
items.e: After the thousands, always write three digits: thirty thousand → 30; four hundred and one → 401. So the number is 30 401.

items.q: Which number is read without the word “hundred”?
items.e: 30 045 has 0 in the hundreds place, so we do not say “hundred”: thirty thousand and forty-five. The others: 30 450 is thirty thousand, four hundred and fifty; 34 500 is thirty-four thousand, five hundred; 30 405 is thirty thousand, four hundred and five.

items.q: How do you write 18 300 in words?
c: one thousand, eight hundred and thirty
items.e: Split off the last three digits: 18 | 300. Read the thousands, then the rest: 18 → eighteen thousand; 300 → three hundred. So 18 300 is “eighteen thousand, three hundred”. Eighteen is 18, not 80.

items.q: Which number is eighty thousand and eighty?
items.e: After the thousands, always write three digits: eighty thousand → 80; eighty → 080. So the number is 80 080.

items.q: 24 050 = twenty-four thousand and ☐. Which word goes in the box?
items.e: Split off the last three digits: 24 | 050. Read the thousands, then the rest: 24 → twenty-four thousand; 050 → fifty. So 24 050 is “twenty-four thousand and fifty”.

items.q: How do you write 15 015 in words?
c: fifteen thousand, one hundred and fifty
items.e: Split off the last three digits: 15 | 015. Read the thousands, then the rest: 15 → fifteen thousand; 015 → fifteen. So 15 015 is “fifteen thousand and fifteen”. Fifteen is 15; fifty is 50.

items.q: Chloe writes “fifty thousand and six” as 5006. What should she write?
items.e: Fifty thousand is 50 | 000. Six goes in the ones place: 50 | 006 = 50 006. 5006 is only five thousand and six: Chloe left out a zero.

items.q: Which number is twelve thousand and twelve?
items.e: After the thousands, always write three digits: twelve thousand → 12; twelve → 012. So the number is 12 012. Twelve thousand is 12 | 000, and twelve is 012 after it.

items.q: How do you write 90 909 in words?
c: ninety thousand, nine hundred and nine
nine thousand, nine hundred and nine
ninety thousand, nine hundred and ninety
items.e: Split off the last three digits: 90 | 909. Read the thousands, then the rest: 90 → ninety thousand; 909 → nine hundred and nine. So 90 909 is “ninety thousand, nine hundred and nine”.

sets.title: Value of a digit and expanded form

items.q: What is the value of the 7 in 37 845?
items.e: The 7 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 7 thousands = 7000. The digit is 7, but its value is 7000.

items.q: What is the value of the 4 in 52 469?
items.e: The 4 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 4 hundreds = 400. The digit is 4, but its value is 400.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 4 is in the ten thousands place, so it is worth 4 ten thousands = 40 000. The digit is 4, but its value is 40 000.

items.q: 40 503 = 40 000 + ☐ + 3. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 40 503 = 40 000 + 500 + 3. The 5 is in the hundreds place, so its value is 500.

items.q: What is the value of the 9 in 94 136?
items.e: The 9 is in the ten thousands place, so it is worth 9 ten thousands = 90 000. The digit is 9, but its value is 90 000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 5 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 5 thousands = 5000. The digit is 5, but its value is 5000.

items.q: In 28 307, the digit 3 stands for ☐.
items.e: Count the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands. The 3 is in the hundreds place, so it stands for 3 hundreds = 300.

items.q: What number is 30 000 + 4000 + 50 + 2?
items.e: Put each value in its place: 3 ten thousands, 4 thousands, 0 hundreds, 5 tens, 2 ones → 34 052.

items.q: What is the value of the 8 in 61 287?
items.e: The 8 is in the tens place, so it is worth 8 tens = 80. The digit is 8, but its value is 80.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 6 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 6 hundreds = 600. The digit is 6, but its value is 600.

items.q: Which shows 62 708 in expanded form?
items.e: Write the value of each digit: 6 ten thousands = 60 000, 2 thousands = 2000, 7 hundreds = 700, 0 tens, 8 ones = 8. So 62 708 = 60 000 + 2000 + 700 + 8. The 0 tens is left out.

items.q: What number is 90 000 + 800 + 1?
items.e: 9 ten thousands, 0 thousands, 8 hundreds, 0 tens, 1 one → 90 801. Write 0 in every empty place.

items.q: In 65 432, the digit 6 stands for ☐.
items.e: Count the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands. The 6 is in the ten thousands place, so it stands for 6 ten thousands = 60 000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 7 is in the tens place, so it is worth 7 tens = 70. The digit is 7, but its value is 70.

items.q: 56 024 = 50 000 + 6000 + ☐ + 4. What number goes in the box?
items.e: The 2 is in the tens place, so its value is 20. 50 000 + 6000 + 20 + 4 = 56 024.

items.q: 52 000 = ☐ thousands. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 52 000 = 52 × 1000, so it is 52 thousands.

items.q: In 44 000, the first 4 is worth how many times the second 4?
items.e: The first 4 is in the ten thousands place: 40 000. The second 4 is in the thousands place: 4000. 40 000 ÷ 4000 = 10. (36 000 is the difference, not how many times.)

items.q: 30 400 = ☐ hundreds. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 30 400 = 304 × 100, so it is 304 hundreds. (30 000 is 300 hundreds, plus 4 hundreds.)

items.q: How many tens are there in 4500?
items.e: 4500 = 450 × 10, so there are 450 tens. (45 is the number of hundreds.)

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the hundreds place: 3 hundreds is more than 0 hundreds. So 54 300 > 54 030.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 10 234 has 5 digits and 9876 has only 4, so 10 234 is greater. A big first digit does not matter when a number has fewer digits.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens place: 5 tens is more than 3 tens. So 24 653 > 24 635. 24 653 is the greatest.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens place: 5 tens is more than 0 tens. So 30 650 > 30 605.

items.q: Which number is between 45 900 and 46 100?
items.e: 45 900 < 46 000 < 46 100. 45 090 is less than 45 900, 46 900 is more than 46 100, and 4600 has only 4 digits.

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: 9999 has only 4 digits. The other numbers have 5 digits, so 9999 is the least, even though it starts with 9.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. Start with the ten thousands: 8 ten thousands is more than 7 ten thousands. So 80 001 > 79 999.

items.q: Put 45 300, 43 500, 45 030 in order from least to greatest.
items.e: All have 4 ten thousands. Thousands: 3 < 5, so 43 500 is the least. 45 300 and 45 030 both have 5 thousands. Hundreds: 0 < 3, so 45 030 < 45 300. Order: 43 500, 45 030, 45 300.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the hundreds place: 6 hundreds is more than 0 hundreds. So 60 600 > 60 060.

items.q: Use each of the digits 3, 8, 1, 6 and 0 once. What is the greatest number you can make?
items.e: Put the greatest digit in the ten thousands place, then the next greatest, and so on: 8, 6, 3, 1, 0. The greatest number is 86 310.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the thousands place: 8 thousands is more than 0 thousands. So 68 009 > 60 809. 68 009 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is greater than 89 000 but less than 90 000?
items.e: 89 500 has 8 ten thousands and 9 thousands, so it is between 89 000 and 90 000. 98 000 and 90 500 are more than 90 000; 8950 is less than 89 000.

items.q: Put 12 100, 12 010, 11 200 in order from greatest to least.
items.e: All have 1 ten thousand. Thousands: 1 < 2, so 11 200 is the least. 12 100 and 12 010 both have 2 thousands. Hundreds: 1 > 0, so 12 100 > 12 010. Order: 12 100, 12 010, 11 200.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens place: 8 tens is more than 7 tens. So 45 687 > 45 678.

items.q: Use each of the digits 3, 8, 1, 6 and 0 once. What is the smallest 5-digit number you can make?
items.e: A 5-digit number cannot start with 0. Put the smallest other digit first: 1. Then 0, 3, 6, 8: 10 368. (01 368 is just 1368, which has only 4 digits.)

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the thousands place: 5 thousands is more than 2 thousands. So 32 510 < 35 102. 32 510 is the least.

items.q: Put 99 000, 100 000, 90 900, 9900 in order from least to greatest.
items.e: 9900 has only 4 digits, so it is the least. 100 000 has 6 digits, so it is the greatest. 90 900 < 99 000 (thousands: 0 < 9). Order: 9900, 90 900, 99 000, 100 000.

items.q: What is the greatest 5-digit number that is less than 50 000?
items.e: Go back 1 from 50 000: 49 999. 50 001 is more than 50 000, 49 000 is not the greatest, and 4999 has only 4 digits.

items.q: Use each of the digits 5, 0, 7, 0 and 2 once. What is the smallest 5-digit number you can make?
items.e: The first digit cannot be 0, so start with the smallest other digit: 2. Then put both 0s, then 5 and 7: 20 057.

items.q: Put 60 606, 66 060, 60 660, 66 006 in order from greatest to least.
items.e: Thousands: 66 060 and 66 006 have 6 thousands; the others have 0. 66 060 and 66 006: hundreds 0 = 0, tens 6 > 0, so 66 060 > 66 006. 60 660 and 60 606: hundreds 6 = 6, tens 6 > 0, so 60 660 > 60 606. Order: 66 060, 66 006, 60 660, 60 606.

items.q:
What is the next number in the pattern?
23 400, 24 400, 25 400, ☐
items.e: Each number is 1000 more: the thousands digit goes up by 1. 25 400 + 1000 = 26 400.

items.q:
What is the next number in the pattern?
15 070, 25 070, 35 070, ☐
items.e: Each number is 10 000 more: the ten thousands digit goes up by 1. 35 070 + 10 000 = 45 070.

items.q: What number is 1000 more than 39 650?
items.e: 39 650 + 1000: 9 thousands + 1 thousand = 10 thousands. Rename them as 1 ten thousand: 3 ten thousands become 4. 39 650 + 1000 = 40 650. (49 650 adds 10 000.)

items.q:
What is the next number in the pattern?
82 360, 72 360, 62 360, ☐
items.e: Each number is 10 000 less: the ten thousands digit goes down by 1. 62 360 − 10 000 = 52 360.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 40 000 to 50 000 there are 10 equal spaces, so each space is 1000. The arrow is 2 spaces after 45 000: 46 000, 47 000. (40 700 counts each space as 100.)

items.q:
What is the next number in the pattern?
30 200, 29 200, 28 200, ☐
items.e: Each number is 1000 less: the thousands digit goes down by 1. 28 200 − 1000 = 27 200. (28 100 takes away 100, and 18 200 takes away 10 000.)

items.q: What number is 10 000 less than 100 000?
items.e: 100 000 is 10 ten thousands. Take away 1 ten thousand: 9 ten thousands = 90 000. (99 000 takes away only 1000.)

items.q:
What is the missing number?
61 800, ☐, 63 800, 64 800
items.e: From 63 800 to 64 800 is 1000 more, so the rule is “add 1000”. 61 800 + 1000 = 62 800.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 0 to 100 000 there are 10 equal spaces, so each space is 10 000. The arrow is 2 spaces after 50 000: 60 000, 70 000. (7000 counts each space as 1000.)

items.q:
What is the next number in the pattern?
47 500, 48 500, 49 500, ☐
items.e: Each number is 1000 more. 49 500 + 1000 = 50 500: 10 thousands are renamed as 1 ten thousand. (40 500 forgets to rename.)

items.q:
What is the rule for this pattern?
56 300, 54 300, 52 300, 50 300
items.e: The numbers get smaller, so we subtract. 56 300 − 54 300 = 2000. The thousands digit goes down by 2 each time. The rule is “subtract 2000”.

items.q:
What is the missing number?
90 450, 80 450, ☐, 60 450
items.e: Each number is 10 000 less: 90 450, 80 450, 70 450, 60 450. Only the ten thousands digit changes. (79 450 takes away 1000.)

items.q: Ali’s school library has 12 450 books. Wei Ming’s school library has 12 540 books. Which is true?
c: You cannot tell which has more
Wei Ming’s library has more books
They have the same number of books
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the hundreds place: 5 hundreds is more than 4 hundreds. So 12 540 > 12 450. Wei Ming’s library has more books.

items.q: A library has 46 800 books. It buys 1000 new books every month. How many books will it have after 3 months?
items.e: Count on in thousands 3 times: 47 800, 48 800, 49 800. (47 800 is after only 1 month, and 76 800 adds 3 ten thousands.)

items.q: Hafiz counts back in ten thousands: 95 200, 85 200, … What is the 4th number he says?
items.e: 95 200 (1st), 85 200 (2nd), 75 200 (3rd), 65 200 (4th). Each time the ten thousands digit goes down by 1. (92 200 counts back in thousands.)

items.q: For a recycling drive, School A collected 38 500 cans. School B collected 10 000 more cans than School A. How many cans did School B collect?
items.e: School B’s bar is School A’s bar plus 10 000. 38 500 + 10 000 = 48 500: the ten thousands digit goes up by 1. (28 500 subtracts, and 39 500 adds only 1000.)

items.q: Mr Tan had $25 000 in the bank. He took out $1000 every month for 4 months. How much money did he have left?
items.e: Count back in thousands 4 times: $24 000, $23 000, $22 000, $21 000. ($24 996 takes away $4 instead of $4000.)

items.q: A park had 64 300 visitors on Saturday and 54 300 visitors on Friday. How many more visitors were there on Saturday?
items.e: The difference is the part marked ?. 64 300 − 54 300 = 10 000: only the ten thousands digit is different (6 and 5). (118 600 adds the numbers.)

items.q: A community centre had 70 000 face masks. It gave out 20 000 masks to residents. How many masks were left?
items.e: The whole bar is 70 000 and one part is 20 000. 70 000 − 20 000 = 50 000 (7 ten thousands − 2 ten thousands = 5 ten thousands). (90 000 adds, and 68 000 takes away only 2000.)

items.q: A charity run had 9000 runners in its 1st year. Each year after that, it had 1000 more runners than the year before. How many runners were there in the 5th year?
items.e: 1st year 9000, 2nd 10 000, 3rd 11 000, 4th 12 000, 5th 13 000. From the 1st year to the 5th year there are only 4 jumps of 1000. (14 000 adds 5 jumps.)
